author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America in US federal records.
The move comes amid escalating trade tensions between the US and Canada following the breakdown of negotiations.
Canadian officials have rejected the name change, with Prime Minister Mark Carney defending the lake's historic name.
Trump can change the name for the US federal government, but cannot compel Canada, private companies or US states to use it.
Canada is also preparing new tariffs on hundreds of American goods, adding to tensions between the two neighbours.

Al Jazeera's Alan Fisher reports from the White House.

description:
Seafood is a staple of local cuisines in Iran's southern coastal cities. But the conflict and US sanctions have made life more difficult for fishermen—and driven costs up for everyone. 
In Bandar Abbas, on the Strait of Hormuz, fishermen face multiple threats: US and Israeli bombing, sea mines, and a US naval blockade. 
Fish market workers say fishermen are afraid to go out due to security concerns, while equipment such as nets and boat gear has become much more expensive. 
Less fuel is reaching the boats, making matters worse resulting in fewer fish being caught and driving up prices. 
Until the dispute over the Strait of Hormuz is resolved, there is too much on the line for many in Iran’s southern coastal communities. 

Al Jazeera's Ferdia Carr reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran's economy had been struggling before the war began, battered by decades of international sanctions and domestic mismanagement. But a raft of new US sanctions is likely to further batter domestic markets. 

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced "Operation Economic Outcast" to "foreclose every other option available to the Iranian regime." 

The new sanctions target sectors including technology, gold, aviation, shipping, and digital assets, weighing heavily on the already weak local currency, which has hit new lows against the US dollar. 

For many businesses, the sanctions mean another setback. 

Nader, a shoemaker in Tehran, said: "The fabric adhesive I used to buy has doubled in cost. 
Even a simple spool of thread has gone up significantly." Narges, another business owner, said her exports to the Gulf states have disappeared.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces has been welcomed by governments across the region, marking a major shift in Syria’s postwar political and military landscape.
SDF commander Mazloum Abdi announced the group would end its existence as an independent military force after completing its integration into the Syrian army.
The SDF once controlled nearly a quarter of Syria, including much of the resource-rich northeast, and was a key US partner in the fight against ISIL.
It also backed a Kurdish-led autonomous administration that operated in the region for about a decade.
That autonomy suffered a major setback in January when Syrian government forces recaptured large areas, prompting an agreement for the SDF to integrate into state institutions.
Former SDF fighters are now being trained to serve in three Kurdish brigades within the Syrian army, while the group’s women fighters are expected to join the Interior Ministry as police officers.

title: Kurdish-led SDF has dissolved, but has Syria really unified its military?

description:
At least 160 people have been killed and hundreds remain missing after flash floods and a landslide struck near Nepal’s border with China’s Tibet region.
The disaster sent a wall of water and mud through the Gyirong border crossing, sweeping away vehicles, buildings and people.
The floods then surged into central Nepal, destroying or submerging villages along the Bhote Koshi and Tri Shuli rivers.
Authorities say hundreds of tourists are among those missing in the popular Himalayan region.
Rescue teams in Nepal and China are searching through mud and debris for survivors and those still unaccounted for.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for an all-out search and stronger early-warning systems to prevent future disasters.
The scale of the destruction is becoming clearer as rescue workers begin a difficult recovery operation.

Al Jazeera’s Ferdia Carr reports.

description:
Renowned Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour has died aged 79, prompting hundreds to gather in Birzeit for his funeral. Born a year before Israel's creation, Mansour became known for works such as ‘Camel of Hardship’ and often used soil, henna and straw instead of Israeli-bought materials. He co-founded a gallery raided by Israeli forces and campaigned for a Palestinian art school, a field once banned by Israeli authorities. His final major piece, ‘On the Wing of an Angel’, is now displayed at the Palestinian Museum.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Birzeit, occupied West Bank.
